goal: Make the built desktop Campaign screens match their FigCraft frames: the Campaigns overview (32/961), the two-panel New campaign & survey screen (212), the assign-contacts grid (324) and the caller roster (645).
outcome: At a desktop viewport the Campaign title rows, stat cards, tables, filter select, form panels, survey panel and roster match frames 32, 212, 324 and 645 in structure, spacing, type and colour, with frame 961's dark parity coming through the existing tokens. /campaigns/new is the two-panel screen the frame draws — Campaign details on the left and the Call-outcome survey on the right, a back control and a single Next action that saves the campaign and its questions. Reports (790/1141) stays out: Epic 3 owns it.

requirements.statement: Design authority is _bmad-output/E-Assets/page-designs/campaign.figcraft: frames 32 and 961 (Campaigns light/dark), 212 (New campaign & survey), 324 (Assign contacts, desktop only) and 645 (Callers). Frame 790/1141 Reports is Epic 3 and must not be built here.

Frame 212 is one screen: a back control, 'New campaign' with its subtitle, a 520px Campaign details panel on the left (name, description, campaign date, time, gap duration, max attempts), an 852px Call-outcome survey panel on the right, and one 'Next' action that saves the campaign and its questions before navigating on.

Frame 32's title row carries a filter select ('All campaigns') beside 'New campaign'; five stat cards (Assigned, Attempted, Reached, Confirmed, Never attempted) sit above a table of Campaign, End Date, Status, Assigned, Reached, Confirmed, Never attempted, with the footer count line.
Frame 645's roster has no add/invite/import control (UX-DR32) and its columns are Caller, Contact, Campaigns, Calls made, Reached, Status, action.
Frame 324 is desktop-only; reuse the repo's grid primitives and campaign components rather than inventing a second visual language, and keep the existing selection/weight/preview/conflict behaviour.
Every colour goes through the existing tokens so frame 961's dark parity holds; measurements come from the frame nodes in document.json, not from a screenshot estimate.
pnpm test:e2e campaign- passes, including the created-campaign flow driven through the two-panel screen.
